name: Art Deco ceramic figures
summary: Slip-cast figures of dancers, bathers, birds and gazelles with long limbs, sharp planes and bold colour. Makers in Vienna, Turin and Bohemia made them in earthenware for the cabinet and the cocktail room.

philosophy.core_thesis: The modern woman, the dancer and the fast animal are stylised into long lines and flat planes, then cast in clay and painted in hard, bright colours.
design_principles: Stylise the body into long, thin limbs and a small head, with a total height of 20 to 45 cm.
Cut the face and the hair into sharp planes, and give the figure a bob or a short cap of hair.
Take the pose from the dance, the swim or the sport: a Charleston step, a diver, a bow with a long scarf.
Cast the figure in earthenware from a plaster mould, and hold the wall at 4 to 6 mm.
Cover the figure with a smooth matt or satin glaze in a few flat colours.
Set two colours in hard contrast: black and ivory, orange and turquoise, silver and red.
Add geometric patterns on the dress: zigzags, triangles, circles and stripes.
Mount a figure on a stepped, geometric base, in black, marble or a glazed block.
anti_patterns: A fussy rococo S-curve with lace and flowers
A naturalistic soft body with a round, doll-like face
A dull grey and brown colour scheme
A glossy pale pastel and a sentimental pose
A thick, heavy folk body with a lumpy glaze
A figure with no base or a plain round base

form.shape: Dancers, bathers, harlequins, women with a dog, birds, deer and gazelles, in thin, tall, stylised forms on geometric bases.
form.profile: A long, sharp line from head to foot, with arms and a scarf that cut sharp angles; animals are drawn as streamlined curves.
form.foot_and_rim: A stepped or wedge-shaped base, flat and heavy, often in black or a bold colour; the underside is flat, glazed and has a mark.
form.proportion: Height 20 to 45 cm; the body is stretched, and the head is about one ninth of the height; the wall is 4 to 6 mm thick.
rules: Stretch the limbs and shrink the head.
Cut the face and the hair in sharp planes.
Use two or three hard colours in flat areas.
Put the figure on a stepped geometric base.
Show a diagonal in the pose: a lean, a step or a flying scarf.

bodies.rule: Use a fine, white to cream earthenware that casts thin and takes a smooth glaze. A hard-paste porcelain serves for the finest figures.

methods: modelling of a master by a sculptor
joining of cast parts with slip
hand painting and spraying of glaze
forming.joins: Arms, scarves and head are cast in separate moulds and fixed with slip. The seams are cut and sponged until the surface is smooth.
forming.details: A hand-painted face with a small red mouth, a vent hole in the base, and a mark of the maker and the model number under the base.

glaze.pattern: Flat colour blocks and geometric patterns on the dress: zigzags, bands, triangles and dots. A face has a painted mouth and a dark brow.
glaze.gloss: Matt to satin, 10 to 50 GU for most figures; a bright colour or a gilt area is higher.
glaze.wear: The matt glaze marks easily with grease, and the gilt wears at the hem. Thin arms, scarves and ears chip.

palette.strategy: A few hard, flat colours that clash on purpose: black and ivory, with orange, turquoise, red and a touch of silver or gold.

firing.kiln: A gas- or coal-fired tunnel or chamber kiln, with a biscuit firing and a glaze firing.
processes: enamel or gilding firing at 700 to 800 °C
firing.scale: A factory with sculptors and decorators, and series of 100 to 1000 figures a model; some figures were numbered limited editions.
firing.signs: A smooth thin glaze, a hand-painted face, a vent hole in the base and a model number with the maker's name.

pieces.form: Dancer in a Charleston step with a flared skirt, on a stepped black base
Woman with a long scarf, leaning, with a bob and a red mouth
Streamlined gazelle on a wedge base, in ivory and black
Woman with a borzoi dog in a stepped pose, with a gilt collar
Bather diving with arms back and a bright swimsuit pattern

positive: sharp planes and a bobbed hair cap
flat bold colour blocks, orange and turquoise

emotion.target_response: Quick, confident glamour: the viewer sees a sharp, long figure in hard colour and thinks of a jazz night, a fast car and the new woman.

use_cases: a 1920s interior or cabaret scene prop
a brief for a stylised dancer figurine
a product design reference for a deco mantel piece
avoid_when: the brief wants a soft, naturalistic figure
the brief wants a folk figure in a lead glaze
the brief needs an unglazed white biscuit

modifiers.how: Change to a hard-paste porcelain body with a clear glaze, add lace and an S-curve pose, and soften the colours.
Change to a hand-built stoneware body, cut the stylised polish and let the hand and the glaze run.
